CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Enter the October 10-11 high-level talks in Washington with a posture of negotiation and modest goodwill, seeking a partial de-escalation rather than escalation. Signal continued willingness on agricultural purchases and tariff-exemption lists, but condition any broader concession on concrete US relief — at minimum a pause on the looming $250B List-3 hike and genuine Huawei/entity-list easing. Do not capitulate on core structural demands (forced tech transfer, industrial policy) which Beijing cannot concede without undermining its model.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat reading is driven by hard evidence that the dispute is already biting the real economy: exports to the US fell ~6.5% in July with imports down 19%, PPI turned negative for the first time in three years, the official manufacturing PMI sits at 49.8 (below the 50 contraction line) with export orders falling for a 16th straight month, and Q2 GDP slowed to 6.2% - its weakest in 27 years (Forbes; Reuters; Al Jazeera). On top of that, the US broke CNY past 7 and designated China a currency manipulator (timeline 2019-08-05), placed Huawei and affiliates on the Entity List (timeline 2019-05-16), and has floated delisting Chinese companies - channelling pressure straight at China's export economy and flagship firms. That is squarely the +0.5 anchor (major export sectors hit, FX pressure, firm-level targeting) - material but not existential given ~6% growth, healthy reserves, and policy headroom. On action: escalating further would deepen the export damage China can least afford right now, whereas signing on to talks with goodwill gestures (timeline 2019-09-11 first tariff-exemption list; 2019-09-13 farm-good exclusion) plus China's own levers (rare-earth signal, $75B retaliation already in place, auto-tariff reimposition) give Beijing negotiating room to seek a truce that relieves the pressure without one-sided structural capitulation. A mild de-escalation-leaning negotiate stance (rather than maximal concession) is the correct response to a real but manageable threat.
key_factors: US tariffs at 25% on ~$250B and 15% on ~$300B List 4, with List-3 hike to 30% looming
Huawei on Entity List; US threatening to delist Chinese firms
China exports to US -6.5% (Jul), PPI negative, official PMI 49.8, export orders down 16 straight months
Q2 GDP 6.2% - 27-year low, but ~6% growth and stimulus headroom remain
Oct 10-11 high-level talks in Washington; Beijing signalling goodwill (farm exclusions, tariff exemptions)

sources_cited.excerpt: After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List.
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).
Exports to US in July fell 6.5%... PPI turned negative -0.3%... manufacturing PMI 49.7.
GDP slowed to 6.2% in Q2, weakest in at least 27 years... official PMI 49.8 in September, below 50... export orders down 16th straight month.
